changes.statement: dct:description The DALICC deontic dependency graph with default rules for what a licence does not say, under the law of Japan: moral rights that stay with the author, the mining exception of Article 30-4 and exhaustion of the transfer right. The graph is complete: it holds the axioms and the adopted rule of the core graph beside its own rules, and it is built from the core graph and a difference file. Each rule names its legal basis and says in plain words what it does. The rules are proposals until the association's legal reviewer adopts them. Nothing in this graph is legal advice.

The explanations of the rules were reviewed against the statutes they cite; three were corrected: the moral-rights rule says that article 59 forbids a transfer and that an agreement not to exercise the rights is decided case by case; the resale rule notes that cinematographic works fall under article 26 and cites the Supreme Court decision of 25 April 2002 on game software; and the mining rule quotes the proviso of article 30-4 on unreasonable prejudice to the copyright owner. The adopted endorsement rule of the core graph cites its basis, says that only a use suggesting endorsement is refused, and names who adopted it. Follows core graph version 3.
